newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Post-expiration trading subdued.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Post-expiration trading subdued.

text.p: Trading in U.S. stock index options was sluggish Monday as some participants relaxed after last week's expiration and underlying markets were rangebound in slow dealings.
"There aren't a lot of people out. There's just not a lot of action," one trader said. "A lot of it is the fact that bonds aren't trading."
U.S. Treasuries were closed for the Martin Luther King Jr federal holiday.
In addition, some attention was diverted to the inauguration of President Bill Clinton for a second term, traders said.
Among underlying markets, the S&P 100 stock index was down fractionally at 761.98 by about 1130 CST/1730 GMT. The index had traded between 760.15 and a record 763.82.
The broader S&P 500 index was up fractionally at 776.48, off its session peak of 777.13, also a record. It hit a session low of 774.19.
The March S&P 500 futures contract added about half a point to 781.35, about in the middle of its 778.30 to 782.40 range.
Traders said fair value for the March contract was 4.50 to 4.60 points over cash, with arbitrage buy programs seen at a 5.80 premium to cash and sell programs at a 3.20 point premium.
Among individual options on the OEX, the February 760 calls and puts were most in demand, with the call trading 3,435 contracts and the put trading 3,860.
Other active OEX puts included the February 740, 745 and 750. Busy calls included the February 775 and 780.
"There is no worthwhile trend (pattern) that the market follows after an expiration day like Friday's," Jerry Hegarty, an analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said in a report.
He noted that last Friday, the last trading day for January contracts, S&P futures traded sharply higher and closed less than a point off their session peak.
Index option premiums remain high, but Hegarty said he expected them to ease a bit Monday. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
